column1: # Dogri word gold set, written 2026-11-18 from the descriptions before the Dogri rules were run on these
# items. Format: word, broad pronunciation(s) separated by |, category, source. R = example word of the
# Dogri phonology descriptions (Bahri 2001, Dogri: Phonology and Grammatical Sketch; Ghai 1991, Studies in
# Phonetics and Phonology, with special reference to Dogri; as cited in the Wikipedia and Wiktionary
# articles on Dogri); N = Dogri numeral as given by U. S. Bahri (2002) in E. Chan's Numeral Systems of the
# World's Languages; C = word of the Dogri locale of Unicode CLDR (common/main/doi.xml, Unicode License v3);
# I = word attested in Dogri text of AI4Bharat IndicCorp v2 (CC0). Pronunciations hand-written from these
# descriptions: a word-initial voiced aspirate is voiceless unaspirated with low tone (grave) on the next
# vowel; an h before a vowel (initial ह, ह after a consonant) is lost with low tone on that vowel; a voiced
# aspirate inside the word is voiced unaspirated, and it or a lost h after a vowel (ह्, the apostrophe, the
# avagraha, final ह) gives high tone (acute) to a stressed vowel before it, else low tone to the vowel after
# it (Ghai); Hindi-type deletion of the inherent vowel; anusvara after a written vowel = nasal vowel, after
# the inherent vowel = homorganic nasal; ऐ औ = ɛː ɔː; ष = ʃ; व = ʋ; a doubled consonant is written double.
# Citation forms with a final ə after a doubled consonant (Bahri: ɪkkə, səttə) are accepted as alternatives.
# Dogri sentence gold set, written 2026-11-18 before the Dogri rules were run on these items. Sentences:
